auth.notes: Account login against the REST host; the token shape was not mapped further because none of it is on the device path — the hardware never contacts any of this, and a local client needs no account.

data_leaves_device: Per-pulse treatment data (flash counts, energy levels, timestamps) uploaded by the phone app
Account identity and profile data (app-side; the app gates its main screen behind login)
cloud.failure_mode: Nothing breaks on the device. The cloud exists solely inside the phone app: account, treatment-history sync, per-pulse upload and malfunction reports. The app itself refuses to start without a network (blocking no-network dialog, login gate), so a cloud shutdown strands THE APP, not the hardware — the device keeps working from its physical controls, and any BLE client built from this spec replaces the app's entire on-device feature set without an account.
hosts: https://ws.silknglobal.com/ (REST: signup/login, treatments CRUD, pair-device telemetry, per-pulse data upload, malfunction reports)
cloud.notes: The app's pair-device call to the cloud is telemetry only — no pairing state, key or authorisation comes back down to the hardware.
cloud.vendor_service: Silk'n cloud (account, treatment history and telemetry for the companion app)

device.name: Silk'n Infinity / Silk'n 7
device.notes:
Home IPL (intense pulsed light) hair-removal devices: the Infinity family (advertising as `Infinity` or `SilknV_F`) and the newer Silk'n 7 (advertising as `Silkn7_App`). The device is fully functional standalone — energy level and flash triggering are physical controls only, and the BLE link is telemetry plus ONE opt-in lock characteristic.
The BLE protocol is unauthenticated: no bonding, no pairing, no challenge, no encryption, and no paywall anywhere in the app. The app counts flashes via notifications, surfaces device errors, polls the skin-color sensor, and can lock the device between sessions if (and only if) the user enabled lock mode in the app. The app CANNOT fire flashes or set intensity — no write path exists to anything but the lock characteristic.
The app itself is account-centric (a blocking no-network dialog at startup, login before the main screen, per-pulse data uploaded to the vendor cloud) but none of that reaches the hardware: the pair-device call to the cloud is telemetry only, and a replacement client needs no account.

exclusivity.recovery: No bond exists to clear, so the worst case is the vendor app holding the connection in the background — close it (or power-cycle the device) and connect again.

pairing.notes: Open GATT: every characteristic in this spec is readable (and the lock characteristic writable) on a bare, unpaired connection, per the app's BLE layer, which never initiates pairing. The only stateful obstacle a replacement client can meet is the app-managed opt-in lock, which is a GATT value, not a pairing state — see the LockUnlockDevice characteristic. Confidence medium: static analysis, not yet confirmed against hardware.

unpair.notes: Nothing to unpair: the link stores no bond on either side, so there is no bond-clearing procedure to document. `supported: false` means 'inapplicable', not 'locked out'.

safety_advisory.detail: This is an IPL/HPL (home pulsed light) hair-removal handset. Used wrongly it can cause permanent harm: burns, blistering, discoloration or scarring of the skin, and serious eye injury from looking into a flash. Always follow Silk'n's own instructions — patch-test first, match the device's energy level to your skin tone, never treat broken, tanned, tattooed or moled skin, and keep it away from the eyes. Over Bluetooth this app reads treatment telemetry and can clear the optional device lock; the flash and its intensity are set on the device itself. This app is EXPERIMENTAL and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Silk'n / Home Skinovations — the manufacturer's manual and safety guidance govern.
safety_advisory.summary: IPL fires intense light pulses — improper use can cause permanent skin burns, scarring, or eye injury.

issued_to_client: Nothing — no pairing, no bonding, no per-device credentials of any kind
stored_on_device: Treatment counters (total pulse count, per-level counters, max-pulses limit)
Lock mode/state (only ever set if a user enabled lock mode in the app; default Released/Unlocked)

factory_reset.description: `unknown`, stated plainly: nothing in the app performs or references a factory reset, and no hardware procedure has been established or tried. The practical good news is that there is almost nothing to reset — the lock clears with one documented write (release_and_unlock), and the counters are cosmetic history, not an adoption barrier.
factory_reset.effect: Unknown whether any owner-accessible reset exists. The state a reset would clear is the treatment counters (total and per-level pulse counts) and the lock mode/state; the companion app contains no reset function and no write path to the counters, so if a reset exists at all it is a physical button procedure nobody has documented.

methods.description: Scan for the exact advertised name `Infinity`, `SilknV_F` or `Silkn7_App`, connect (no pairing), subscribe to the TreatmentDynamicInformation and DeviceErrors characteristics, and optionally clear the app-managed lock with one write. The device needs nothing else.

steps.action: Power on the device and scan for one of the exact local names `Infinity`, `SilknV_F`, `Silkn7_App`.
steps.expect: Advertisement matching one of the three names (the name selects the telemetry layout — see protocol_details).

steps.action: Connect. No pairing or bonding is requested or required.
steps.expect: GATT service 720411ac-adfe-2015-0820-835742ad3835 with five characteristics, plus standard DIS (0x180A).

steps.action: Read LockUnlockDevice (...9033). If it reports Locked, write 30 30 (Released + Unlocked) once.
steps.expect: Lock reports Released/Unlocked and does not re-engage.

steps.action: Enable notifications on TreatmentDynamicInformation (...9011) and DeviceErrors (...9022).

setup.notes: Nothing to provision — no network, no account, no credentials. The device advertises under one of three exact local names and accepts a bare BLE connection from any central. Confidence medium: read from the app's BLE layer (scan filter, connection and subscription sequence), not replayed here.

rejoin.notes: There is nothing to rebind: no bond is stored on either side, so a new phone or client simply scans and connects. The only residue a previous app install can leave behind is the opt-in lock — if the old client locked the device on disconnect, write release_and_unlock (30 30) once from the new one.

testing.notes: No hardware on the bench. All protocol facts were recovered by static analysis of the vendor's Android companion app (v6.1, 2026-08); nothing has been replayed against a device and no over-the-air capture exists yet. One HCI snoop of a single treatment session would confirm the opcode set, the telemetry endianness and the lock default.

artifacts.description: Static analysis of the companion app (2026-08). Source of every protocol fact here: the exact-match scan filter on the three advertised names, the primary service and its five synthetic characteristics, both TreatmentDynamicInformation layouts and their name-based selection, the DeviceErrors code range, the 2-byte lock/unlock semantics and the app's lock-on-disconnect behaviour, the every-20-pulses color-sensor poll, the cloud hosts, and the negative findings — no bonding or auth anywhere, no write path to flash firing or intensity, no billing/paywall code, no OTA/DFU path.
No hardware unit, HCI capture or third-party implementation was available. The ~40 device user-manual PDFs bundled in the app's assets were noted as a manual source but not mined for this spec.

helpful_urls.description: The vendor companion app this spec was recovered from (analysed at v6.1, versionCode 38). Account-gated and cloud-centric, but everything it does with the hardware is reproducible from this spec without an account.

covers: Per-pulse telemetry: total flash counter, per-level counters, current energy level, max-pulses limit (notify, 20-byte frames)
Skin-color sensor readings: raw and threshold RGB (read, polled by the app every 20 pulses)
Lock/unlock — clearing the app's opt-in lock with one write
not_covered: Firing flashes or setting the energy level — no BLE write path exists for either; both are physical-control-only by design, so a replacement app is telemetry-only just like the vendor's
Firmware update — no OTA/DFU path was found in the app
Resetting the on-device treatment counters — no such command was found
local_access.summary: Fully local by design: the device works standalone from its physical controls, and the complete BLE surface (telemetry, errors, skin sensor, lock) is open GATT with no pairing, no auth and no account — every documented function is reachable from any BLE host using this spec alone.

protocol_details.control_surface: Lock/unlock is the ENTIRE write surface. No opcode to fire a flash, request a pulse, or set the energy level exists anywhere in the app; energy levels are physical-button only. This is a safety property of the hardware design as much as a protocol fact — a replacement app is telemetry-plus-lock, exactly like the vendor's.
protocol_details.lock_semantics: The lock is advisory and app-managed, not a security feature: it exists so the app can prevent flashes between supervised sessions, it is opt-in (default off), and any client can clear it with a single unauthenticated write. The mode byte is the durable half — Released (0x30) tells the firmware to ignore the lock state — so writing 30 30 once is a permanent clear from the client's point of view. Whether every Infinity firmware revision honours mode=Released is unconfirmed.

treatment_dynamic_information.infinity_layout: Advertised name `Infinity` or `SilknV_F`: big-endian — u8 opcode @0, u32 max_pulses @1, u32 total_counter @5, u8 current_level @9, then five u16 per-level counters @10/12/14/16/18 (see the characteristic `format`).

session_flow.description:
Post-connect sequence, as the app drives it: 1. Connect (no pairing) and read LockUnlockDevice (...9033). 2. If the user enabled lock mode, the app writes Locked here and
   re-locks on disconnect; it writes Unlocked from its
   treatment-start and treatment-finish screens. A replacement client
   can instead write release_and_unlock (30 30) once and ignore the
   lock thereafter.
3. Enable notifications on TreatmentDynamicInformation (...9011) and
   DeviceErrors (...9022); a 20-byte frame arrives per pulse.
4. Poll ColorMeasurements (...9055) every 20 pulses; read DeviceIO
   (...9044) for button state and DIS 0x2A25 for the serial.
session_flow.verification_note: Read from the app's BLE layer; no capture and no hardware replay yet.

treatment_dynamic_information.silkn7_layout: Advertised name `Silkn7_App`: little-endian variant of the same header fields, with the per-level counters OMITTED from the payload — the app increments its own per-level tallies whenever a notification arrives with opcode==1 (per-pulse event). A replacement client must do the same to keep per-level statistics on this variant.
treatment_dynamic_information.variant_selection: The 20-byte TreatmentDynamicInformation frame has two layouts, chosen by the advertised local name the client connected to. A client must keep the scan-result name, not just the address.

remaining_unknowns: TreatmentDynamicInformation opcode values beyond 1 (0 is likely a status snapshot) — needs one HCI capture of a treatment session

format.name: opcode
format.notes: Only opcode 1 is established. 0 is likely a status snapshot — inferred, needs one capture.

format.name: max_pulses
format.notes: Lifetime flash capacity of the lamp/cartridge.

format.name: total_counter
format.notes: Total flashes fired over the device's life.

format.name: current_level
format.notes: Currently selected energy level (set by the device's physical button — never over BLE).

characteristics.name: TreatmentDynamicInformation
characteristics.notes: 20-byte frame, notified once per pulse. TWO layouts exist, selected by the advertised local name; the `format` below is the Infinity/SilknV_F (big-endian) layout. Devices advertising `Silkn7_App` use a little-endian variant in which the per-level counters are omitted from the payload and incremented app-side on each opcode==1 (per-pulse) event — see protocol_details.treatment_dynamic_information for that variant. Byte 19 is unused/unknown in both layouts.

characteristics.name: DeviceErrors
characteristics.notes: Five u8 error-code slots. Codes observed in the app's handling span roughly 10–70 and cover: high-voltage subsystem, temperature, fan, ignition, color-sensor calibration, stuck buttons, checksum, and micro-current faults. The exact code-to-fault table is not fully recovered — see remaining_unknowns. A zero slot means no error.

lock.description: Lock mode + Locked state: what the app writes between sessions when the user enabled lock mode. Useful only for replicating the vendor app's behaviour; a local-control client has no reason to send it.

release_and_unlock.description: Released + Unlocked: clears the app-managed lock and sets the mode that keeps it cleared. The one write a replacement client should issue on first connect if the device reads back Locked.

characteristics.name: LockUnlockDevice
characteristics.notes: The ONLY writable characteristic, and the whole of the app's control surface. Two bytes: a mode byte (0x30 Released / 0x31 Lock) and a state byte (0x30 Unlocked / 0x31 Locked). The lock is opt-in and app-managed: the app locks the device between sessions only if the user enabled lock mode, unlocks from its treatment-start screen, and re-locks on disconnect. A never-paired device ships Released + Unlocked. A replacement client that writes 30 30 (Released + Unlocked) once is never bothered by the lock again. Whether the firmware honours mode=Released on every Infinity revision is the one open question here.

format.name: button_state
format.notes: bit7 = trigger pressed, bit6 = function button pressed; other bits unknown.

characteristics.name: DeviceIO
characteristics.notes: One byte of physical-control state; bit 7 set while the trigger is pressed, bit 6 while the function button is pressed. Read-only snapshot — buttons cannot be driven over BLE.

format.name: threshold_r
format.notes: Red threshold the firmware compares against; endianness unconfirmed.

characteristics.name: ColorMeasurements
characteristics.notes: Skin-color sensor: seven u16 values — raw RGB and threshold RGB triplets plus a seventh value whose meaning is not established. The app polls this every 20 pulses (the sensor gates whether a flash is safe; the enforcement is on-device, the readout is informational). Endianness of the u16 fields is NOT established — confirm against hardware before decoding.

services.name: Silk'n Hair Removal Service
services.notes: The only application service. Its five characteristics are synthetic constants sharing the 12345678-9012-3456-7890-1234567890xx prefix and ending 11/22/33/44/55. No encryption, no authentication, no handshake: subscribe and read. There is exactly ONE writable characteristic (the lock); the app cannot fire flashes or set intensity, and neither can any other client — no such opcode exists.

services.name: Device Information Service (standard)
services.notes: Standard DIS (0x180A); only the serial number string is used by the app.
